title: Hebrew Calendar
intro: The fixed Hebrew calendar is lunisolar, with Anno Mundi year numbering and calculated month lengths.
structure: Ordinary years have twelve months. Seven years of the nineteen-year cycle have thirteen months because a second Adar is inserted. The leap years are 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 19.
pattern_note: Months contain 29 or 30 days; some lengths depend on postponement rules for the year start.
example: Passover falls in Nisan, around Northern Hemisphere spring. Intercalating Adar maintains the seasonal alignment.
history: The fixed rabbinic calculation developed over centuries and is used for Jewish religious dates. Religious days traditionally begin at sunset.
model: This provider owns the deterministic 19-year calendar and postponement rules. ICU/CLDR supplies locale-sensitive formatting rather than defining the date arithmetic.
limits: It does not reconstruct earlier local new-moon observations or specify the timing of every local religious observance.
